mutants.description: An invalid capacity is silently clamped to 1 instead of raising, so callers never learn their configuration was wrong.
mutants.search_block:
if capacity < 1:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be >= 1")

mutants.description: The miss counter starts at 1 instead of 0, so every cache reports a miss that never happened.
len(cache) reports one entry fewer than the cache actually holds.
Successful reads are counted as misses and hits are never incremented, so hit-rate monitoring is exactly inverted.
Reading a key marks it as the oldest entry instead of the newest, so hot entries are evicted first.
Overwriting an existing key silently keeps the old value, so updates are lost.
A cache filled exactly to capacity evicts an entry it should have kept, losing data one insert early.
Invalidating a key leaves it in the cache with a None value, so the slot still counts against capacity and hit statistics.
invalidate_prefix returns the number of entries left in the cache instead of the number removed.
Prefix invalidation also removes keys that merely contain the prefix in the middle, deleting unrelated entries.

mutants.replace_block: doomed = [key for key in self._data if prefix in key]

mutants.description: The last page claims a next page exists, so UIs render a 'next' button that leads to an empty page.
per_page=0 no longer raises a clear error and instead blows up with a raw ZeroDivisionError.
Page counts round down instead of up, so the final partially-filled page is dropped and trailing items become unreachable.
The page number stored on the result is one less than requested, so page 1 is reported as page 0 and navigation highlights break.
Page.total reports the number of items on the current page instead of the whole collection, breaking any 'showing X of Y' display.
A trailing number without a unit like '1h30' is silently treated as seconds instead of raising an error.
mutants.search_block:
if number:
        raise ValueError("trailing number without a unit: %r" % text)

mutants.description: Only the last unit group is counted, so '1h30m' parses as 30 minutes and the hours are dropped.
Keys keep their surrounding whitespace, so 'a =1' and 'a=1' become two different keys.
Values containing '=' like 'query=a=b' now crash the parser, although only the first '=' is meant to split.
A price of exactly zero is rejected as invalid, so free items cannot be priced.
A max_discount of 0 is ignored, so 'cap the discount at zero' lets the full discount through.
Results are rounded to four decimal places instead of two, so prices carry sub-cent fractions.
A limit of 0 raises an error instead of returning an empty string.
Text that is exactly `limit` characters long gets needlessly cut and suffixed instead of being returned unchanged.
